gaps.quote: the convolution of two vectors becomes a pointwise (entry by entry) product of their transforms
gaps.note: The page uses 'the convolution of two vectors' without defining it. The only convolution it names is the radix-digit convolution, a different notion, so the reader cannot tell which vector operation is meant.

gaps.quote: Transforming, multiplying pointwise, and inverting therefore computes the convolution.
gaps.note: The claim that transform, pointwise product and inverse compute the convolution, 'up to the factor q', is presented as following from the preceding facts. The page does not say which way the factor q goes or show the calculation, so the reader cannot check it.

gaps.quote: The reason is that $\sum_{j=0}^{q-1} \omega^{j(k-l)}$ equals $q$ when $k = l$ and $0$ otherwise, a geometric sum over powers of $\omega$.
gaps.note: The page says the map is invertible and gives its inverse, justified only by this sum. The reader is not shown the geometric-sum formula, why the sum vanishes for k not equal to l (which needs omega^m not equal to 1 for negative m as well as 0 < m < q), or how substituting y into the inverse formula gives x once the 1/q factor cancels against the q from the sum.
